newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli shells kill woman in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shells kill woman in south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli and allied militia forces shelled three south Lebanon villages on Tuesday, killing a civilian woman and wounded two other people, Lebanese security sources said.

The shelling was an apparent breach of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon last April and bars the south Lebanon combatants -- Hizbollah and Israeli and its allied militia -- from targeting civilian areas.

The sources said Naeemeh Hallal, in her 30s, was killed and another woman was wounded when shells rained down on the village of Habboush facing Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. A man was wounded when shells hit near the village of Arab Salim.

The bombardment, which also hit the village of Kfar Roummane, was in retaliation for guerrilla shelling of three posts of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia in the zone, SLA sources said.
There was no report of casualties in the attack on the SLA.
In Beirut, foreign ministry sources said Lebanon will lodge a complaint over Tuesday's shelling with a five-nation committee monitoring breaches of the ceasefire understanding.

The understanding that ended the Israeli blitz which killed some 200 people, mostly civilians, bars Israel and Hizbollah from targeting civilian areas but allows raids on Israeli forces in the zone and gives both sides the right to self defence.
Security sources said the Hizbollah guerrillas fired more than 50 mortar bombs at the SLA posts on the edge of the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep zone and opposite Habboush and Kfar Roummane.
Tuesday's civilian fatality was the first in south Lebanon this year.
"The woman was killed when a shell hit her house in Habboush square. About 40 shells have slammed so far into the village and its outskirts," one security source told Reuters.
"In Kfar Roummane, a shell hit near the school and children started running," the source added.
The pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for the attack on the three SLA posts saying in a statement in Beirut that its fighters were able to achieve direct and accurate hits.
It said guerrillas, an hour after the first attack, fired at the Ahmadiyyeh post manned by Israeli and SLA forces. There was no immediate confirmation of that reported attack.
Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to oust them from the south Lebanon zone occupied to prevent cross-border attacks on northern Israel.
Tuesday's shelling came hours after the ceasefire monitors ended a day-long meeting on Monday to discuss Lebanese and Israeli complaints over alleged breaches of the understanding.

The Lebanese complaint was over an Israeli air raid last week which wounded a civilian shepherd in eastern Lebanon while Israel complained its forces found five bombs planted by a road near the village of Beit Lif in the south Lebanon zone.

"The Monitoring Group by unanimity deemed it necessary to urge once more all combatants to abide strictly and fully by the provisions of the April 26, 1996 understanding and to adopt restraint and caution in military operations in the vicinity of civilian populated areas," the monitors said in a statement.

The group comprising the United States, France, Lebanon, Israel and Syria said it accepted both incidents as factual. The monitors meet at the coastal headquarters of the UNIFIL peacekeepers in Naqoura in the south Lebanon zone.
